---
title: Limber Angular Power Spectra
---

This page describes how [[numcosmo|NcXcorKernel]] computes the window $W_\ell(k)$ under the
Limber approximation.

The Limber approximation is activated by `NcXcorKernel:l-limber`. Its value
$\ell_\mathrm{limber}$ divides the multipoles: those with $\ell \ge \ell_\mathrm{limber}$
take the Limber path, and those below take the non-Limber path of [UltraLevin: Non-Limber
Angular Power Spectra](../../ncm/specfunc/sbessel_projection.qmd). The value 0 puts every
multipole on the Limber path, and -1 puts none.

The two paths differ in a single step. In both, each component of a kernel has a radial
kernel $K(\chi,k)$, its radial integral $I_\ell(k)$ (Eq. (2) of the UltraLevin page) and a
prefactor $p_\ell(k)$, and its window is $W_\ell(k) = p_\ell(k)\, I_\ell(k)$. The
non-Limber path computes $I_\ell(k)$ as a Levin integral; the Limber path replaces it by a
closed form in $K$. After that step the paths are the same: $W_\ell(k)$ is represented over
$k$ as in [The window over k](../../ncm/specfunc/sbessel_projection.qmd#the-window-over-k),
and a pair of windows is integrated as in [The outer
integral](../../ncm/specfunc/sbessel_projection.qmd#the-outer-integral).

The Limber path also requires the radial kernel of each component to be a product of two
factors,
$$
K(\chi,k) = K_\chi(\chi)\, K_k(\chi,k),
$$
with $K_\chi$ a function of the distance alone and $K_k$ the factor that depends on the
wavenumber. For the galaxy clustering component of [[numcosmo|NcXcorKernelGal]], $K_k$ is
$\sqrt{P(k,z)}$ at the redshift $z$ of $\chi$. The component evaluates $K_\chi$ with
[[numcosmo|nc_xcor_kernel_component_eval_window]], $K_k$ with
[[numcosmo|nc_xcor_kernel_component_eval_kfactor]] and $p_\ell$ with
[[numcosmo|nc_xcor_kernel_component_eval_prefactor]]. The factorization is what lets the
multipoles of a block share the evaluations at one distance, as described below.

Throughout, $\nu_m \equiv m + 1/2$ and $\nu \equiv \nu_\ell$.

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.ticker import FormatStrFormatter
from numcosmo_py import Nc, Ncm

Ncm.cfg_init()
plt.rcParams.update({"figure.dpi": 110, "axes.grid": True, "grid.alpha": 0.3})

cosmo = Nc.HICosmoDEXcdm.new()
dist = Nc.Distance.new(5.0)
dist.prepare(cosmo)
ps = Ncm.PowspecAnalytic.new(
    Ncm.PowspecAnalyticShape.BBKS, Ncm.PowspecAnalyticGrowth.LCDM
)


def gauss_window(l_limber: int, ell: int) -> Nc.XcorKernelIntegrand:
    """The window of a Gaussian kernel at one multipole, exact or under Limber."""
    sbi = Ncm.SBesselIntegratorLevin.new(ell, ell)
    kernel = Nc.XcorKernelAnalyticGauss.new_full(dist, ps, 1500.0, 300.0, 4.0, sbi)
    kernel.set_l_limber(l_limber)
    kernel.set_reltol(1.0e-8)
    kernel.prepare(cosmo)

    return kernel.get_eval_vectorized_full(cosmo, ell, ell, sbi)
```

## The Limber form of the radial integral

The Limber approximation expands the radial integral in $1/\nu$, assuming that $K$ is
smooth in $\chi$; the terms beyond the leading one involve derivatives of $K$ in $\chi$
[@Loverde2008]. The leading term is $K$ at $k\chi = \nu$ times the integral of the weight,
$$
\int_0^\infty j_\ell(x)\,\mathrm{d}x = \frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2}\,
\frac{\Gamma\big((\ell+1)/2\big)}{\Gamma\big(\ell/2+1\big)}
\simeq \sqrt{\frac{\pi}{2\nu}},
$$
where the last form differs from the Gamma ratio by a relative amount of order $1/\nu^2$
(0.9% at $\ell = 2$, $6 \times 10^{-6}$ at $\ell = 100$). For the weight $j_m$,
$$
\int \mathrm{d}\chi\, K(\chi,k)\, j_m(k\chi) \simeq I^\mathrm{L}_m(k),
\qquad
I^\mathrm{L}_m(k) \equiv \sqrt{\frac{\pi}{2\nu_m}}\,\frac{K(\nu_m / k,\, k)}{k},
$$
with a relative error of order $1/\nu_m^2$. So $I_\ell(k) \simeq I^\mathrm{L}_\ell(k)$. The
index $m$ is general because the derivative weights below need $I^\mathrm{L}_{\ell+1}$ as
well.

$I^\mathrm{L}_m(k)$ is $K$ evaluated at the single distance $\chi_m = \nu_m / k$. Since $K$
vanishes outside its support $[\chi_\mathrm{min}, \chi_\mathrm{max}]$,
$I^\mathrm{L}_m(k)$ vanishes outside the band
$$
\frac{\nu_m}{\chi_\mathrm{max}} \le k \le \frac{\nu_m}{\chi_\mathrm{min}}.
$$
Where $K$ is nonzero at an end of its support, $I^\mathrm{L}_m$ is discontinuous at the
corresponding end of the band: nonzero on one side, zero on the other.

@fig-limber-exact shows the two windows the library builds for a Gaussian kernel, one from
the Levin integral of [UltraLevin: Non-Limber Angular Power
Spectra](../../ncm/specfunc/sbessel_projection.qmd) and one from $I^\mathrm{L}_\ell$.
Their largest difference, relative to the peak of the window, is proportional to $1/\nu^2$
for large $\nu$.

```{python}
#| label: fig-limber-exact
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Top: the window W_l(k) of a Gaussian kernel (mean 1500 Mpc, width 300 Mpc, cut at
#|   4 sigma) at l = 10 and l = 100, from UltraLevin (solid) and from the Limber form
#|   (dashed, a darker shade drawn over it), each divided by the peak of the UltraLevin
#|   window; at l = 100 the two coincide to 5.6e-3 of the peak. The k range shown is where
#|   either window exceeds 1e-3 of its peak. Bottom: the largest
#|   difference between the two windows over k, divided by that peak and multiplied by
#|   nu^2. The difference is 1.26 of the peak at l = 2, 5.6e-3 at l = 100 and 6.6e-4 at
#|   l = 300; times nu^2 it tends to a constant (56 at l = 100, 60 at l = 300).
#| code-fold: true
ells = np.array([2, 3, 5, 10, 20, 30, 50, 100, 200, 300])
shown = {10: ("C0", "#0b3c5d"), 100: ("C1", "#8c3b00")}
scaled = []
q_lo, q_hi = np.inf, 0.0
fig, axs = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(8, 6.0))

for ell in ells:
    levin = gauss_window(-1, ell)
    limber = gauss_window(0, ell)
    k_lo, k_hi = levin.get_range()
    ks = np.geomspace(k_lo, k_hi, 2000)
    w_levin = np.array([levin.eval_array(k)[0] for k in ks])
    w_limber = np.array([limber.eval_array(k)[0] for k in ks])
    peak = np.abs(w_levin).max()
    scaled.append(np.abs(w_limber - w_levin).max() / peak * (ell + 0.5) ** 2)

    if ell in shown:
        color, shade = shown[ell]
        visible = (np.abs(w_levin) > 1.0e-3 * peak) | (np.abs(w_limber) > 1.0e-3 * peak)
        q_lo = min(q_lo, ks[visible].min() / (ell + 0.5))
        q_hi = max(q_hi, ks[visible].max() / (ell + 0.5))
        axs[0].plot(ks / (ell + 0.5), w_levin / peak, color=color, lw=2.0,
                    label=rf"$\ell = {ell}$, UltraLevin")
        axs[0].plot(ks / (ell + 0.5), w_limber / peak, color=shade, lw=1.0, ls="--",
                    label=rf"$\ell = {ell}$, Limber")

axs[0].set_xscale("log")
axs[0].set_xlim(q_lo, q_hi)
axs[0].xaxis.set_major_formatter(FormatStrFormatter("%g"))
axs[0].xaxis.set_minor_formatter(FormatStrFormatter("%g"))
axs[0].set_xlabel(r"$k / \nu$  [$R_{H0}^{-1}$]")
axs[0].set_ylabel(r"$W_\ell(k)$ / peak")
axs[0].legend(fontsize=8)
axs[1].plot(ells + 0.5, scaled, "o-", ms=4)
axs[1].set_xscale("log")
axs[1].set_xlabel(r"$\nu$")
axs[1].set_ylabel(r"$\nu^2 \times$ largest difference / peak")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
